page: Microsoft Azure L32s_v3 is a storage-optimized server belonging to the LSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of 8008 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. There are no GPUs present on this server.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory metrics. The Intel Xeon 8370C processor achieved a PassMark CPU score of 37006.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14250.0. Memory performance is a relative strength, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25% at 2845.43, supported by a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 1680.1 GB/sec. Database operations on PassMark scored 15226.69, and Redis SET operations reached 31.46 million operations per second, both falling within the average range.

While the server handles smaller workloads efficiently, such as text generation with a 135M parameter LLM model which scored in the top 25% at 292.02 tokens per second, it exhibits significant performance degradation on larger models. Large 70B parameter LLM inference prompt processing and text generation fell into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Given the massive 8008 GB NVMe SSD storage capacity, 256.0 GB of RAM, and average database performance, this server is configured for storage-intensive workloads, database hosting, and data warehousing rather than large-scale machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure L32s_v3 is a storage-focused server from the LSv3 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. It features 256.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 8008 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPUs. Benchmark results place its compute and database capabilities in the average range, including a PassMark CPU score of 37006.88 and Redis SET throughput of 31.46 million operations per second. However, its memory subsystem performs strongly, scoring in the top 25% on PassMark. Tradeoffs are evident in large-scale machine learning, where 70B LLM text generation drops to a poor 2.27 tokens per second. This hardware profile is suited for large database deployments, storage-heavy applications, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring high local storage density.
